title: Group Sex
description: More than three people changes the arithmetic of attention in a specific way: individual focus becomes structurally impossible, anonymity within the group becomes possible, and the quality of abundance — multiple bodies, multiple responses — is its own distinct experience.
equipment: A group of consenting adults who have explicitly agreed; a clear prior conversation with your partner about limits.
safetyNote: Consent to each new contact should be confirmed — presence in the group is not general permission. Have a signal with your partner that means you want to stop or leave.

instructions.label: As a solo participant
instructions.content: Go in as a single person joining an existing arrangement rather than arriving as part of a unit. Your structural position is different: you're a single node in a network, not one half of a couple managing a shared experience. Notice how you navigate contact and choices without a partner's presence as a reference point, and what the absence of that shared anchor changes about how you move through the encounter. Notice also what the scale itself produces — whether the number of people changes how you make choices, and whether the abundance or the ambient quality of the group context carries its own charge independent of individual contact.

instructions.label: With a partner
instructions.content: Go in with your partner and with the question genuinely open rather than a predetermined expectation. Notice what a group context produces differently from one-on-one or three-person encounters: whether the multiplicity of options changes how you make choices, whether the reduced ability to focus fully on any one person changes the quality of each contact, and whether the ambient sexuality of multiple people in shared space produces something independent of direct contact. Debrief with your partner afterward as specifically as possible — what did each experience, and what did the scale of it produce that smaller arrangements hadn't?

explore: Does the number of people change how you make choices — do you become more selective, less, or differently oriented?
Is there a specific quality of the group context — anonymity, abundance, the ambient sexuality — that produces something smaller arrangements don't?
Does the reduced individual attention — the structural impossibility of full focus on any one person — change what each contact produces?
What does the experience tell you about how important focused attention versus multiplicity of sensation is for you specifically?
why: Group sex differs from smaller arrangements primarily through scale: at a certain number, individual focus becomes structurally impossible and the experience shifts from a network of specific connections to something more like immersion in collective sensation. For some people this is exactly what they're seeking — the loosening of the one-to-one structure, the particular anonymity that becomes possible within a group, the abundance. For others, the absence of individual focus makes each contact feel less significant, and they discover that attention matters more to them than variety. Which is true is only available from direct experience, because most people's imagination of what group sex is like turns out to be quite different from the actual experience in one direction or another.
